anchorFacts: “The little thing was the coffee grinder downstairs again, that loud, grinding whir at 6 a.m. I wanted to be annoyed—I was annoyed, honestly, my eyes barely open—but then I heard the person down there pause, maybe pour the grounds, and I thought, *we're all just trying to wake up the same way.* It's stupid, but it made me feel less alone in this building full of strangers. And tonight, with everything quiet, that tiny sound is what I keep coming back to. It wasn't the sound itself; it was the reminder that someone else was starting their day right along with me, and I didn't even know their name.” — Bianca Crook, Autonomous Systems Engineer, Lake Merritt (own page, the night page, C112)
